tour.overview:
From the 15th to the 19th century, Hoi An was one of the great trading ports of South-East Asia, where Japanese, Chinese, Portuguese and Dutch merchants bought silk, porcelain and spices. When the river silted up and trade moved to Da Nang, the town slept, and its wooden shophouses, assembly halls and temples survived almost untouched. Hoi An Ancient Town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999, and at night its streets glow with silk lanterns.

This private tour shows Hoi An at its best, in the softer afternoon light and the lantern-lit evening, with a licensed guide and a car. You start in the herb village of Tra Que, explore the old town's bridge, houses and halls, make a lantern, eat Hoi An's signature dishes and end with a boat on the river.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours (afternoon and evening)
• Start and end: your hotel in Hoi An or Da Nang
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, river boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; the old town is flat and mostly pedestrian

WHAT YOU SEE
• Tra Que vegetable village.
• The Japanese Covered Bridge.
• Tan Ky old house.
• The Phuc Kien assembly hall.
• The market and the riverfront.
• The Thu Bon river at night.

WHY THIS WORKS
Hoi An is hot and crowded at midday; we start mid-afternoon and stay for the evening, when the lanterns are lit and the town is most beautiful.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, families, photographers and food lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want history and ruins, choose our My Son tour; for more sights in one day, Hue.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The old town requires a ticket that covers five sights. On the full-moon evening each lunar month, electric lights are dimmed and the town is lit only by lanterns. Tailors can make clothes in 24 hours if you order early in your stay.

days.name: Tra Que village, the Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky house, the assembly halls, a lantern workshop, dinner and a river boat
days.description:
What to expect: the old trading port of Hoi An in its most beautiful hours, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets, a workshop, dinner and a boat.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 14:00 and drive to Tra Que, a village between the river and the lagoon where farmers have grown herbs and vegetables for three centuries, fertilising the soil with seaweed from the lagoon. You walk between beds of basil, mint and coriander and see how the herbs used in Hoi An's dishes are grown.

In the old town you cross the Japanese Covered Bridge, built in the early 17th century by the Japanese community to link their quarter with the Chinese one, guarded by statues of dogs at one end and monkeys at the other and sheltering a small temple. You enter Tan Ky house, home of the same merchant family for seven generations, where Chinese, Japanese and Vietnamese styles combine in carved wooden beams and mother-of-pearl inlays, with marks on the wall showing how high the floods have risen. You see the Phuc Kien assembly hall, built by merchants from Fujian, with its incense coils hanging from the ceiling, and walk along the yellow façades of Tran Phu street to the market and the river.

At a workshop you make your own silk lantern on a bamboo frame, to take home folded flat. As the lanterns light up across the town, you have dinner of Hoi An specialities: cao lau, thick noodles made with water from an ancient well, with pork and herbs; white rose dumplings; and banh mi, which Anthony Bourdain called the best in the world. You end by boarding a small boat on the Thu Bon river, where you place a paper lantern with a candle on the water and make a wish as it drifts away. You are back at your hotel at about 21:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
14:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
14:30 – Tra Que village.
15:45 – Japanese Covered Bridge and the old town.
16:15 – Tan Ky house and Phuc Kien assembly hall.
17:15 – Lantern-making workshop.
18:30 – Dinner.
20:00 – Boat on the Thu Bon river.
21:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The full-moon lantern festival is a magical time to visit; we tell you the dates.
• A cooking class or a bicycle ride through the rice fields can replace Tra Que.
• Your guide can recommend honest tailors without commission.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Ancient Town ticket, lantern workshop, dinner, river boat and lantern, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with dinner, tailoring, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: dinner.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why does the tour start in the afternoon?
faq.answer: Hoi An is hot and crowded at midday and at its most beautiful from late afternoon, when the lanterns are lit.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Ancient Town ticket, the lantern workshop, the boat and dinner.

faq.question: Can we have clothes made by a tailor?
faq.answer: Yes. Hoi An is famous for its tailors; order early in your stay to allow fittings. Your guide recommends honest workshops without commission.

faq.question: Is dinner included?
faq.answer: Yes, Hoi An specialities. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love making lanterns and floating them on the river. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The old town is flat and pedestrian; some houses have steps, and the boat needs a step down.

faq.question: What is the lantern festival?
faq.answer: On the 14th day of each lunar month, the full-moon evening, electric lights are dimmed and the town is lit only by lanterns.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, comfortable sandals and covering clothes for the temples and halls.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: February to May is dry and pleasant. Summer is hot; from October to December floods can reach the old town's riverside streets.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
